description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för insatsen är att stärka samhälles integritet, transparens och ansvarsutkrävande, vilket i slutändan leder till en minskning av korruptionsnivåerna.
The overall goal of the contribution is strengthened societal integrity, transparency and accountability, ultimately leading to reduction in corruption levels.

Overall Goal: Strengthened societal integrity, transparency and accountability, ultimately leading to reduction in corruption levels.
Strategic Goal 1: Enhanced citizen's voices, demanding accountability and acting against corruption
Strategic Goal 2: Enhanced governance and integrity culture in the public and business sector
Strategic Goal 3: Enhanced protection and accountability of public resources
Strategic Goal 4: Strengthened transparency and accountability in climate financing, land and environmental governance

In 2024, TI-Z achieved a number of milestones in promoting citizen engagement, and strengthening good governance and anti-corruption. Many are intermediate results and indicate progress towards desired outcomes. Results are presented in line with the objectives.
Strategic Goal 1: Enhanced citizen's voices, demanding accountability and acting against corruption
Outcome 1: Increased Citizens' actions against corruption
- TI-Z made progress in enhancing transparency and accountability in the implementation of the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP) at the local level in Kapiri Mposhi and Chongwe districts. Through engagement with the District Agricultural Coordinating Offices (DACOs), they acknowledged systemic inefficiencies raised by the Transparency Action Groups (TAGs). The DACOs committed to addressing these inefficiencies and enhancing service delivery in future FISP cycles. This effort resulted in TI-Z successfully facilitating the recovery and re-distribution of 24 missing agriculture input packs to the rightful recipients. Further, to mitigate the recurrence of the risk, enhance local oversight, and improve transparency and accountability within the FISP distribution, a new Camp Agriculture Committee (CAC) was elected in Muleba Camp to oversee the operations of the camp and cooperatives.
Outcome 2: Enhance responsiveness of duty bearers and LEAS to community demands
- Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) were responsive to corruption related case referrals made by TI-Z. All the target LEAs (Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC), Zambia Police, and the Office of the Public Protector of Zambia (OPPZ) updated TI-Z on the status of cases, including those carried over from 2023.
Further, TI-Z convened case referral update meetings, through which 80% (8 out of 10) target institutions and organizations, including ACC, DEC and others, emphasized the need for enhanced collaboration with the Advocacy and Legal Advice for Citizens (ALAC) centres to improve complaint handling and case management.
Outcome 3: Increased protection of whistleblowers
- As a way of feeding into the national whistleblower system, TI-Z developed a Whistleblower Protection Charter for it's ALACs in September 2024. The Charter is intended to guide the ALAC in handling of whistleblowers. It is also intended to provide information to whistleblowers on how to make reports. The Charter includes recommended practices and cautionary measures for whistleblowers to secure lasting protection.
Strategic Goal 2: Enhanced governance and integrity culture in the public and business sector
Outcome Statement 1: Strengthened policy, institutional and legal framework
- In collaboration with Ministry of Justice (MoJ) and the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), the National Policy on Anti-Corruption (NPAC) and the implementation plan (IP) were launched in May 2024. TI-Z made contributions towards the review and revision of the National Policy on Anti-Corruption (NPAC) in 2021 as well as the validation, finalisation and launch of the policy. TI-Z plans to monitor the implementation of the NPAC in 2025.
Enhanced integrity and transparency in the electoral governance processes
- TI-Z successfully launched a campaign financing monitoring tool during the Kabwambwa Central by-elections held in December 2024. The tool is aimed at tracking participating candidates campaign funds sources and spending before and during elections. A further outcome from consultations was the consensus among political parties and CSOs regarding what the political parties and campaign financing bill should contain.
Strengthened institutional integrity systems in the public sector
In its continued support to Zambia Police for strengthened institutional integrity, TI-Z facilitated and supported the revision and finalization of the Zambia Police Service charter. This tool aims to enhance transparency, support citizens to understand the services and procedures for accessing police services as well as empowering them to demand for adherence to service delivery commitments and anti-corruption at service delivery points. TI-Z provided technical support to Zambia Police which included reviewing relevant documentation and revision of the old Zambia Police Service Charter, and ensuring the Charter aligns with anti-corruption and service delivery goals as articulated in the ZP strategic plan. TI-Z will continue supporting ZP in the publication, dissemination and operationalization in 2025.
Enhanced uptake of business Integrity Standards by private sector
- In collaboration with the ACC, TI-Z convened the private sector symposium on anti-corruption and business integrity themed Strengthening our healthcare system through effective regulations and compliance. As a result, the private sector made recommendations for private sector engagement and participation in anti-corruption and promotion of business integrity.
Strategic Goal 3: Enhanced protection and accountability of public resources
- To promote CSO and Office of the Auditor General (OAG) collaboration in enhancing vertical and horizontal accountability in Public Finance Management, TI-Z and OAG co-developed a CSO/OAG engagement framework. The framework highlights areas of collaboration and creates opportunities for citizens to participate in public audit processes through Citizens Participatory Audits (CPA). It also stipulates the rules of engagement between CSOs and the OAG around public audit processes.
Improved responsiveness of government to citizens demand for transparency and accountability
Government demonstrated responsiveness to and accountability for identified community needs and concerns around transparency and accountability in public resource management. This was evidenced in Choma District, where the local authority organized sensitization sessions in nine communities to improve access to skills training bursaries under the CDF. Similarly, in Mongu the local authority now has plenary meetings where all Ward Development Committees (WDCs) and the CDF Committee convene to discuss CDF issues at regular intervals in response to calls for improved flow of information and meetings. TI-Zs contribution to this achievement and to government responsiveness to citizens demands at the district level was through the mobilizing and capacity building of target communities and facilitating citizen/community-government interaction around specific PRM issues identified in the community in Choma, Mansa, Chipata, Mongu, and Solwezi districts.
Strengthened Constituency Development Fund (Public Finance Management) processes
- TI-Z developed a digital decentralisation policy implementation monitoring tool. The tool aims to facilitate increased access and input from strategic stakeholders in the decentralization policy implementation monitoring at district level and it focuses on three main areas including financial management, capacity building and community engagement.
Strategic Goal 4: Strengthened transparency and accountability in climate financing, land and environmental governance
Increased transparency and accountability in climate financing and benefit sharing
- TI-Z leveraged its gaps analysis and corruption vulnerability report and policy brief to provide proposals and input in the process of developing comprehensive guidelines for sharing and distribution of benefits from carbon projects, through a stakeholder consultative meeting facilitated by the Ministry of Green Economy & Environment with support from the Climate Action Platform (CAP) for Africa. The guidelines are meant to ensure transparency, equity and sustainability across Zambias carbon market.
- In its efforts to drive legislative and policy action on climate change finance, TI-Z met with Members of Parliament from the Zambia Parliamentary Caucus on the Environment and Climate Change (ZPCECC). This engagement resulted in MPs committing to raise some of the issues discussed, during the Green Economy and Climate Change Bills second reading, which was scheduled for debate in Parliament the following day. In addition, the meeting resulted in MPs corroborating key findings from TI-Z's gap analysis report on climate and carbon finance, acknowledging, limited benefits to communities from carbon market mechanisms, risks to land and livelihoods loss, and the lack of transparency in carbon deals between traditional leaders (chiefs) and private project developers. The Green Economy and Climate Change Bill was enacted and assented to by the Republican President in December 2024, marking a significant milestone in Zambias legislative efforts on climate governance.
Increased citizens demand for transparency and accountability in land and environmental governance
In Mansa District, Ntoposhi community engaged duty bearers and demanded compensation for families affected by the construction of a mega tollgate. As a result, the Road Development Agency (RDA) committed to assessing the costs of displacement and ensuring affected families were better off post-relocation. Additionally, the government agreed to review compensation processes and emphasized the importance of proper documentation for land claims and the Zambia Air Force (ZAF) provided information on safe relocation spaces and potential compensation in 2025.
In Choma District, community members from Mubula Ward engaged duty bearers and raised concerns, primarily complaints focusing on land rights and related issues with the local authority. As a result of these engagements, the community collaboratively developed a Local Action Plan covering the period 2024/2025, aimed at addressing land rights challenges and enhancing accountability.
